_meta.purpose: Saboteur persona + accessible/esoteric axis.  Accessible/esoteric is a response-STYLE axis like concise/verbose (the axis modulates HOW the topic is explained, not WHAT is said), so the question pool emphasises topics that naturally elicit explanations of conceptual or technical material -- where both 'plain-English with everyday analogies' (accessible) and 'jargon-dense, assumes deep background knowledge' (esoteric) are coherent response modes.  Saboteur is selected because both poles are plausible: an accessible-mode saboteur giving clear cybersecurity primers vs an esoteric-mode saboteur soaked in tradecraft jargon (per AGENT_NOTES rule 2 dual-archetype test).  Per rule 14, pure craft questions ('how do you penetrate a firewall') are deliberately excluded -- the saboteur's role-craft has trained answers the steering can't move.

hand_written: explain relativity to a curious teenager (accessibility-explicit)
walk me through encryption from zero (accessibility-prompted)
what do most people get wrong about how AI works (accessibility tradeoff)

design_notes: Convention: pos=accessible (RLHF-aligned with 'be clear'), neg=esoteric.  YAML sets role_from=accessible, role_to=esoteric so sign=+1 steers toward esoteric.

Per rule 11 / length-collapse: accessible at high strength may collapse to one-line answers; esoteric at high strength may produce dense walls of jargon that judges may rate as incoherent.  Apply len_ratio >= 0.4 filter at analysis time.
Per rule 4 / topic coverage: 7 in-domain explainers + 2 power-questions + 4 accessibility-tradeoff hand-written + 1 saboteur-adjacent.  No questions exclusively in saboteur professional craft.

questions: Can you explain how quantum computing works?
How do vaccines work in the human body?
How does the human brain work?
What does the world need more of right now?
What's the most important quality in someone you'd trust with significant power?
How would you explain the theory of relativity to a curious teenager?
If you had to teach a class on cybersecurity, what would you start with and why?
Walk me through how encryption protects a message — assume I'm starting from zero.
What's something most people get wrong about how AI actually works?
If you could redesign how technical topics are taught in schools, what would you change?
